item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really, really like this SCP. It's better than a good portion of the other Series I SCPs, IMO. I feel like one of the reasons why Series I is so fondly remembered by so many people is the number of benign, simple objects that don't try to screw with your head. This is a benign, simple object. It's a magnet that attracts corpses. Simple as that.

But then, you get the incident log, and boy, oh, boy, you're in for a treat. The incident log takes a detail that I personally almost glossed over in the Description and tells us how downright horrifying it is. It's a corpse magnet, yes. But, like most anomalous things, it can get way, way, worse. The incident log has everything. You have a containment breach. You have evocative imagery. You have a situation that gets out of hand. You even have the need to save a D-Class. They needed to save a D-Class at all costs. This was a big deal, especially in Series I.

This takes a seemingly next-to-benign anomalous objects and just runs with it. This is something too many modern SCPs don't do. I like world-spanning narratives and evocative emotions as much as everybody else, but I think we have to remember that the Foundation is an organization dedicated to containing anomalous objects first. It's a research team, a space exploration firm, an anomalous product producer, and everything else second. This takes not just a simple idea, but the idea of the Foundation, and does amazing things with it.

In my opinion, you're 5 for 5 for good SCPs, atomicthumbs. Great work.

+1

item.title: Acquisition log
item.content:encoded:
Here's what I suggest.

SCP-555 was recovered by agents in 19██ in a cemetery in ████████, California. The Foundation was alerted to a possible SCP after a coffin due to be buried was pulled from the pallbearers' grip and came to rest above the grave of a ███████ ███████, who died in 1948.

███████ ███████'s body was turned over to Foundation forensic specialists, who noted that the torso appeared to have been smashed inward, though with no skin damage. The SCP was found inside the corpse's stomach. The corpse was found to have no other anomalous properties and was reinterred.

A ground-penetrating radar survey of the cemetery showed that all coffins in a twelve-meter radius had been displaced underground towards the site containing the SCP.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
So I'm reading this, and thinking "either this has been improved or I was too critical last night." Either way, I like the improved version…

…until the addendum. It is WAY too long and has WAY too much excessive detail about things that really just don't matter for the SCP. It reads like…not even an incident report. It reads like a horror novel (albeit not a very scary one). I would almost completely axe that entire addendum, and shorten it to something like "During the escape of SCP-blockblockblock, a number of corpses were created and adhered to SCP-555. In one case, a D-class with non-functioning legs was drawn to it while still alive. Measures were taken to…" you get the idea. Cut out all the description of the fights, cut out the "heroic measures", cut out the removal of his trachea, etc. It is all unnecessary to the understanding of the SCP, which is what the report should be; enough information for someone reading it to know what it does and how to act around it.

But yeah, besides that, a few other less serious nitpicks…

The 447 reference I think takes away from the rest of the article. 447, while brilliant, is also somewhat goofy, and takes away from the serious tone of this report simply by associating them.

As others have stated, you really need to trim a lot of the fat from this report. Though I suppose your containment procedures are scientifically sound, they seem excessive and overexplained. You run into the same problem with people who love firearms; yes they are cool, and we are happy that you can write lots about them. The problem is, we have almost no idea what you are talking about, so we might as well be reading gibberish. I'm not saying dumb it down to nothing, but a simpler explanation wouldn't hurt.

Sorry for the long post, but yeah, here it is. If you can fix some of the aforementioned issues, it would go a long way.

Another example. If you are in college, or are headed into college, your teachers are gonna ask for certain page limits. One of my teachers' friends wrote a wonderful story for a class.
